data.narrative:
Theseus is a Seed-stage Defense & Security company founded by a team with Stanford mechanical engineering and McGill/Yale software research credentials, having raised $4.3M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 10 companies spanning both stages: 2 public entities (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms including UFORCE, Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, and Saronic.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement to the $4.3M raised proxy, implying a $11M valuation. Peer-median analysis across 5 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a $1.0B median valuation, with a range spanning $125M (NODA AI, Series A) to $4.0B (Stark Defence, Series A). The peer set reflects significant valuation dispersion within Defense & Security at both Seed and Series A stages.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $9M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $505M. This wide spread reflects material uncertainty inherent to early-stage defense-tech valuation. Key drivers of outcome uncertainty include product-market validation, regulatory pathway clarity, and customer acquisition trajectory—none of which are quantified in current data. The stage-progression floor and peer-median ceiling diverge substantially, suggesting that comparable maturity, technical differentiation, and customer commitments will be critical determinants of realized valuation.
